title: Start with your library
summary: Cueport reads your Serato library or builds a local library from your music files on your computer. Your music and library data remain local.

items.title: Serato library.
items.text: Read crates, subcrates, tracks, hot cues, BPM, key, colors, comments, and beatgrid markers from your local _Serato_ folder.

items.title: Cueport Direct.
items.text: Add music files instead of linking Serato. Cueport keeps the audio in place and stores collections, cues, notes, colors, restore points, and analysis in its own database.

items.title: Local analysis.
items.text: Compute BPM, key, waveform columns, and beatgrid markers from audio on your machine.

title: Send music to your phone
summary: Pair the phone app with your computer over the local network, then send selected collections and tracks to the phone for browsing and playback.

items.title: Local playback.
items.text: Play tracks from local files while browsing collections, with waveform context, cues, and beatgrid markers alongside the player.

items.title: Cue points and notes.
items.text: Add or edit hot cues and notes whether you use Serato or Cueport Direct.

items.title: Phone companion.
items.text: Send selected collections to the phone app, cache tracks for playback, and send phone edits back to the paired computer for review.

title: Review before publishing
summary: Cueport queues edits in a local working layer so you can review what changed before updating Serato files or keeping Cueport Direct changes in its database.

items.title: Local editing layer.
items.text: Cueport marks pending edits so you can see what changed across tracks and collections.

items.title: Publish on approval.
items.text: Serato edits write back to MP3s and crate files only when you choose to publish. Cueport Direct edits remain in their own database.

items.title: Backups and restore points.
items.text: Cueport creates safety copies before updating Serato. Cueport Direct manages edits and restore points in a separate database.
